claims.head: Hughes gets company tonight
claims.call: The Stars’ L2 (Robertson, Hintz and Seguin) spends at least 51% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Stars keep sending Robertson’s line (Robertson, Hintz and Seguin) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Glen Gulutzan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Devils’ first line is Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt.

notes.text: Johnathan Kovacevic was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Declan Chisholm.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Esa Lindell is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Thomas Harley has taken his spot beside Miro Heiskanen.
Matt Duchene is on long-term injured reserve (abdomen injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.

DAL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Stars
DAL.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately, and the Stars will be without Lindell. The Stars can tip it if they get good looks.

NJD.head: Leaning the Devils’ way
NJD.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately, and the Stars will be without Lindell. The Stars can still swing it if they get good looks.

story.head: The Stars are rolling
paras: The Stars have won four straight. The Devils have won two in a row.

It’s strength against strength: the Devils are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Stars are one of the best at keeping shots away. At home, Glen Gulutzan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ first line.
